en: This is the private home of Mayor Gilbert.
Kindly call during normal hours.
That's what comes of living where you work.
You'd do well not to act too suspiciously.
Oh, hello there.
note: Shared with Wilfred (pawnbroker, msgs 177122/177551).

en: Paying house calls? What a busy man you are.
You might as well help me with my work.
I'm surprised... or rather, lost for words.
Could it be you have no sense of direction?
Yet oddly, I can't seem to get angry
note: #152 '...' follows.

en: You're certainly an interesting fellow.
, it's you.
note: After #608 'Oh, ' + name: 'Oh, {NAME}, it's you.'

en: Well, all right. Do come in.
I'll allow your visiting habit as a quirk.
Strangely, I can't bring myself to dislike you.
Being a politician by trade, I'm usually
wary of other people, you know
note: #152 '...' follows.

en: Hahaha, that's just like you.
I won't say another word. Come whenever
you please, my amusing friend.
To make even the man who governs London
my servant... What good fortune.
Y-you
note: #152 '...' follows: 'Y-you...'. Shared with Maud (msg 267486, before the name on the next line).

en: Still, why are humans so utterly
unguarded... It's beyond me.
A few talks, and they open their hearts to me.
You
note: #152 '...' follows: 'You...'. Shared with Sylvia (msg 280626).

en: I knew it
note: No used_in in the slice; msg 25764 (Gilbert): 'You... / I knew it' + pause dots.

en: Heh heh heh, this is going nicely.
Victory
note: No used_in in the slice; msg 25796: 'Victory' <pause> 'will be mine...' (auto space after the pause).

en: will be mine
note: After #829 'Victory' and a pause; #152 '...' follows.

en: Ah, I'm sorry.
note: Gentle player; also Bradford 59124, Nick 189999/190064.

en: I just wanted to come and greet you
note: #152 '...' follows.

en: Hello, Mayor Gilbert. It's me,
note: Gentle version of #767: 'Hello, Mayor Gilbert. It's me, / {NAME}. Don't you remember me?'

en: . Don't you remember me?
I'm terribly sorry about the other day.
<Yes, that's right>
note: Answer choice (no used_in): gentle version of #780, reply to #778/#779.

en: <I have my reasons>
note: Answer choice (no used_in): gentle version of #781 (same English).

en: Let's talk for a little while
note: Pause dots follow: 'Let's talk for a little while...'

en: It's no use telling you this, but...
note: No used_in; msg 26053 shows it between #838 and #840 (own line). Ends with '...' so #840 can start a sentence (the decoder also shows #840 as the start of msg 26090).

en: People don't see me as an upright politician.
Yet this city needs someone who does
the kind of work I do.
That is why I work on as mayor.
note: Echoes #795 'I believe that, and so I work on as mayor.'

en: Let those who want to talk, talk.
They have every right to speak, but
they can do nothing more than that.
This work is what I live for.
It has to be me, and no one else
note: #152 '...' follows.

en: You're certainly an interesting fellow, though.
I'd like you to help me with my work, too.
Your orders, please
note: #152 '...' follows. Colin/Abraham as servants (after #754 ', my master...' or #4253).

en: What on earth is happening to me?
I'm more worn out with every passing day.
, my master.
Give me any order you wish
I'm sure I fall asleep in my bed, but then
I wake up on the sofa in the living room.
Hold it right there, you.
I haven't seen you before. And so early, too.
State your name.
I am no one suspicious.
note: Stern player (as #930).

en: My name is
note: Before the name; #863/#363/#473 give the full stop.
After the name. Variant '' where it follows dots ('...' + '。'), so no fourth dot.

en: I have only just come to London, however.
Hmm... I see. Very well.
I'm Constable Colin. No suspicious behavior.
note: #955/#956 (slice 012) split the same text over two rows; shortened here to fit one line.

en: Any trouble just means more work for me.
How long are you going to hang about here?
Well, well...
I keep running into you these days.
An early-morning stroll? How commendable.
Though you look rather pale for it.
, good morning.
note: After the name (Colin, Peter, Dean, Ted, Mary): '{NAME}, good morning.'

en: Have you seen or heard anything odd?
This city's become a dangerous place lately.
Good grief, I can't watch it all on my own.
Wandering about here? That's suspicious.
What district are you from? State your name.
I am certainly no one suspicious.
